simple.meaning: נְחַת (nᵉchath) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to descend ; causatively, to bring away , deposit , depose.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 5:15. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְחַת (H5182) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נְחַת (nᵉchath) / H5182 is traced through Ezra 5:15, Ezra 6:1, Ezra 6:5, Daniel 4:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

structuredEvidence.definition: to descend ; causatively, to bring away , deposit , depose

firstOccurrence.englishText: He said to him, ‘Take these vessels, go, put them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let God’s house be built in its place.’

timeline.evidenceText: He said to him, ‘Take these vessels, go, put them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let God’s house be built in its place.’
Then Darius the king made a decree, and the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon, was searched.

Also let the gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple which is at Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, be restored and brought again to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place. You shall put them in God’s house.
Thus were the visions of my head on my bed: I saw, and behold, a tree in the middle of the earth; and its height was great.
The tree that you saw, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the earth;
But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him.
